# herdr-gitview

[Permalink: herdr-gitview](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#herdr-gitview)

[![CI](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/actions/workflows/ci.yml)[![Release](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/9f2cb410523e63a42268577c86132871a25ac452d925b89631a6cd47fda26b34/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f6769746875622f762f72656c656173652f43686d617261582f68657264722d67697476696577)](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/releases/latest)[![License](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/e742cfd0ad7a8582d6e8d39bdd67385bddeb24b527ee15d141a6050ccc5fb399/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f6769746875622f6c6963656e73652f43686d617261582f68657264722d67697476696577)](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/LICENSE)

[features](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#features) · [install](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#install) · [quick start](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#quick-start) · [keys](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#keys) · [configuration](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#configuration) · [limitations](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#limitations) · [changelog](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

A git view for the [Herdr](https://herdr.dev/) app. Review what your agent
changed: the changed files in the Changes panel, a syntax-highlighted diff
beside them. Press `Enter` and the diff pane _becomes_ your real nvim, at the
line you're on. You never leave Herdr.

Tip

Using the **herdr TUI** (terminal)? Its guide is [TUI.md](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/TUI.md).

![image](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/32128755/698082003-5dd57c9c-fad9-41af-8959-dda3fabc750c.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.REDACTED.REDACTED)

> **Pairs well with**
>
> - [herdr-nvim](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-nvim): a persistent nvim sidebar, one key away
> - [herdr-chat](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-chat): a native chat for Pi, Claude Code and Codex

## Features

[Permalink: Features](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#features)

- **Takes over the Changes panel** \- the tab bar's **Changes** button (or
`cmd-shift-g`) shows gitview's file list for the space you're in, and a
click opens the file's diff in a full-height pane right beside it. Moving
through the list, the diff follows.
- **Grouped changes** \- conflicts, staged, and unstaged changes in separate
sections, flat or as a folder tree, with `+ added −deleted` counts per file
and in total.
- **Stage, discard, commit inline** \- `s`/`u`/`x` or the `+``−``↺` buttons
on a file, a folder or a whole section; discards confirm first. Write the
commit message right in the panel (`shift+enter` for more lines) and
commit what's staged, or everything when nothing is.
- **Readable diffs** \- syntax highlighting (dark or light, to match your
app theme), added and removed lines tinted in the theme's colors,
word-level emphasis on edited lines, and collapsible context folds.
- **Preview** \- markdown renders, images show, and a changed image shows
before and after side by side. One click switches back to the diff.
- **Edit in real nvim** \- `Enter` turns the diff pane into your nvim, at the
line ( [herdr-nvim](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-nvim)'s when it's
installed). `:q` brings the diff back. Moving to another file swaps nvim
for that file's diff again; with unsaved changes nvim stays.
- **Commit history** \- `l` opens the log; pick a commit to browse its files
and diffs. `w` filters it to the commits your branch added.
- **Knows what your branch was cut from** \- branch scope diffs against the
branch you actually branched off ( [Branch scope](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/TUI.md#branch-scope)).
- **Review notes to any agent** \- select diff lines, write a note under them,
and send the batch into the input of any agent in Herdr. It types, without
the clipboard; you decide when to press enter.
- **A tab of its own** \- `cmd-g` opens gitview in a tab for the repo you're
in: the diff on the left, the list on the right.
- **Remote spaces** \- in a space on another machine, git runs there.
- **Mouse support** \- click, double-click to open, drag-select diff lines,
hover buttons.

## Requirements

[Permalink: Requirements](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#requirements)

- The **Herdr desktop app** (herdr-app ≥ 0.1.12).
- **git** on `PATH`.
- An editor for `Enter`: [herdr-nvim](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-nvim),
else nvim, vim, `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR`, or the system's default app.
- macOS. Linux should work but is untested; Windows isn't supported.

## Install

[Permalink: Install](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#install)

With the Herdr app open:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
```

It downloads the prebuilt gitview for your machine, checks it, adds its
mods, adds `cmd-shift-g` and `cmd-g` where they're free, and puts gitview in
the Changes panel. No git clone, no Rust. Or ask the agent in your Herdr
window to "add the mod at github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview".

- **Update:** run the same command again.
- **Uninstall:** the same command with `--uninstall`; the stock Changes
panel comes back.

## Quick start

[Permalink: Quick start](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#quick-start)

1. **Open it.** Press **Changes** in the tab bar, or `cmd-shift-g`. The
space's changed files show in the panel.
2. **Browse.** Click a file, or `j`/`k`: its diff opens in a full-height pane
beside the panel and follows your selection.
3. **Edit.**`Enter` turns the diff pane into nvim at the line. `:q`, and
you're back on the diff.
4. **Stage & commit.**`s` to stage (the file moves up), `x` to discard (asks
first), `c` to write the commit message, `enter` to commit.
5. **See what your branch did.**`w` switches to "vs the base branch"; `l`
opens the log filtered to your branch's commits.
6. **Review for your agent.** In the diff, drag over lines (or `v` +
`j`/`k`), `a` to write a note, `enter` to save it. `p` → pick an agent →
the notes land in its input.

The footer shows the keys that work right now; `?` lists them all.

## Keys

[Permalink: Keys](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#keys)

| Key | Where | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cmd-shift-g` | anywhere | Show or hide the Changes panel with gitview (Linux: `ctrl-alt-shift-g`) |
| `cmd-g` | anywhere | gitview in a tab of its own; again to go back (Linux: `ctrl-alt-g`) |
| `j` / `k`, arrows | list, diff | Move; in the list the diff follows |
| `enter` | list, diff | Open the file in the editor at the line |
| `s` / `u` / `x` | list, diff | Stage, unstage, discard |
| `c` | list | Write the commit message (`enter` commits, `shift+enter` new line) |
| `t` | list | Flat or tree |
| `w` | list | Uncommitted or vs the base branch |
| `l` / `n` | list | History / notes |
| `J` / `K` | diff | Next / previous file |
| `v`, `a` | diff | Select lines, write a note |
| `p` | list, diff | Send the notes to an agent |
| `m` | diff | Diff or Preview |
| `?` | list, diff | All keys |

## Configuration

[Permalink: Configuration](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#configuration)

gitview reads the same `config.toml` as the TUI plugin,
`~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/chmarax.gitview/config.toml`. In the app
these apply: `editor`, `base`, `context_lines`, `show_untracked` and
`view_width_percent` (the diff pane's width). See
[TUI.md](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/TUI.md#configuration) for each key. Colors follow the app's theme.

## Limitations

[Permalink: Limitations](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#limitations)

- **nvim is the editor gitview knows** \- with herdr-nvim's nvim or your own
nvim, gitview checks for unsaved changes and closes it for you. Other
editors open the file too; you close them yourself.
- **Notes attach to working-tree changes** \- you can't annotate historical
commits.
- **herdr-nvim on remote spaces** \- in a space on another machine, Enter
starts a plain editor there instead.

## Development

[Permalink: Development](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview#development)

```
git clone https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview
cd herdr-gitview
herdr-app/install.sh               # builds from source and installs into the running app
herdr-app/install.sh --uninstall
```

`cargo test` runs the engine's tests and `node --test herdr-app/test/*.test.mjs`
the mods'. The e2e suites in `herdr-app/e2e/` (`run.sh`, `coexist.sh`,
`follow.sh`, `jank.sh`, `reload.sh`, `package.sh`) drive a private app in the
background. How the mods are built: [herdr-app/RECIPE.md](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/blob/main/herdr-app/RECIPE.md).

A [Herdr](https://herdr.dev/) plugin that names your tabs and panes from what
they are doing: the Git branch, the running process, or the topic of a Claude
Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, Hermes or Antigravity session. No LLM, no external
service, and a tab you rename yourself stays yours.

## Install

[Permalink: Install](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#install)

You need Herdr 0.8.2+ on macOS, Linux or Windows.

```
herdr plugin install kryptamine/herdr-auto-title --ref stable
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

`stable` is the latest release. On amd64 and arm64 the install downloads its
binary; elsewhere it builds from source with Go 1.24+. On Windows the download
needs Git for Windows' Bash, and Go without it. The second line starts the
plugin now rather than at Herdr's next start.

To update, keeping your configuration:

```
herdr plugin update herdr.auto-title
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

Herdr before 0.9.4 has no `plugin update`; rerun the install lines instead.
An update stays on the ref you installed: a tag never moves, and no `--ref`
follows `main`. To switch, install once with `--ref stable`.

To run the latest commit on `main`, which can be ahead of the latest release,
leave `--ref` out. Herdr then builds from source with Go 1.24+:

```
herdr plugin install kryptamine/herdr-auto-title
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

## Herdr desktop app

[Permalink: Herdr desktop app](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#herdr-desktop-app)

The [desktop app](https://herdr.dev/) has no plugins, so Auto Title runs there
as a service of its own, started at every login on macOS, Linux and Windows.
The mod installs it on all three platforms; Windows needs no Git Bash or Go.

**With the mod:** ask the app's agent to add the mod in this repository's
[`mod/`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/mod) folder, or copy `mod/mods/auto-title` into
`~/.config/herdr-app/mods/` and merge [`mod/keys.json`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/mod/keys.json) into
`~/.config/herdr-app/keys.json` yourself. `cmd-alt-t` opens a popup; press
`Install`. In a tab of its own it downloads the binary of the release the mod
belongs to, checks it against `SHA256SUMS` and has it install itself. The same
popup starts and updates it. Once a day the service asks GitHub whether a
newer release is out, and opens the popup by itself once for each one. To
remove Auto Title, have the service's copy uninstall itself:

```
# macOS
~/Library/Application\ Support/herdr-auto-title/bin/herdr-auto-title desktop uninstall
# Linux
"${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/herdr-auto-title/herdr-auto-title" desktop uninstall
```

**By hand:** with a release binary, or one built with `make build`:

```
./herdr-auto-title desktop install     # start now and at every login
./herdr-auto-title desktop uninstall   # stop it and remove it
```

On Windows the popup prefers Git Bash and uses Windows PowerShell 5.1 when
Git Bash is unavailable. If policy blocks PowerShell scripts, install Git for
Windows or use a release binary directly. No Go installation is needed.

On Windows the binary is `herdr-auto-title.exe`, and the service is a Task
Scheduler task; its copy is
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\herdr-auto-title\bin\herdr-auto-title.exe`, which
`desktop uninstall` removes too.

Installing again is the update. The service runs its own copy of the binary, so
the one you ran can be deleted. Its log is `~/Library/Logs/herdr-auto-title.log`
on macOS and `journalctl --user -u herdr-auto-title` on Linux. On Windows it
keeps no log; run `herdr-auto-title.exe desktop` in a terminal to see one.

What differs from Herdr TUI:

- Only tabs are named: the desktop app has no pane labels or workspace topics.
- The service does not see your shell's environment, so settings go in
[`config.env`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#configuration), never in a shell profile.
- `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_ICONS` needs a Nerd Font as the app's `ui_font` in its
`settings.json`, since the tab bar is drawn in that font.

## Recommended setup

[Permalink: Recommended setup](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#recommended-setup)

Three settings make Auto Title work as intended. Each is optional.

**Create tabs without a name prompt.** Herdr asks for a name before it creates
a tab, and a name typed there counts as your own, so Auto Title never names
that tab. In Herdr's `config.toml`:

```
[ui]
prompt_new_tab_name = false
```

**Install Herdr's integration for each agent you use.** It tells Auto Title
which session a pane holds, so the tab is named after that session. Without it,
a tab says only what the agent puts in its terminal title, and for Antigravity
CLI that is nothing but `agy`.

```
herdr integration install claude           # Claude Code
herdr integration install codex            # Codex
herdr integration install antigravity-cli  # Antigravity CLI
herdr integration install grok             # Grok Build
herdr integration install hermes           # Hermes Agent
herdr integration install pi               # Pi
```

**Show the topic in the sidebar.** Auto Title reports what each workspace's
active tab is doing as `$topic`, and Herdr draws it only where a sidebar row
asks for it. This keeps the name and branch on top, with the topic in bold
under them:

```
[ui.sidebar.spaces]
rows = [\
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "branch", "git_status"],\
  [{ token = "$topic", bold = true, dim = false }],\
]
```

Each client reads its own `config.toml`, so set the rows on every machine you
attach from.

## What you get

[Permalink: What you get](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#what-you-get)

```
~/work/dashboard                       →  1 · dashboard
~/work/dashboard on feature/MC-13200   →  2 · dashboard › MC-13200
nvim editing auth.provider.ts          →  3 · nvim › auth.provider.ts
an agent working on OAuth scopes       →  4 · dashboard › Implement OAuth scopes
ssh into prod-01                       →  5 · ssh › prod-01
mosh into devbox                       →  6 · mosh › devbox
$HOME                                  →  7 · Shell
```

- The number in front is the tab's position, which is also the key that
switches to it.
- The default branch is left out. Other branches are cut down to what
identifies them: `bugfix-asa-cpanel-uapi-mc-13675` becomes `MC-13675`.
- A tab with several panes is named after the pane focused in it, whether the
tab is shown or not. `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT=true` names it after its
agent pane instead.
- Each pane gets a name of its own, so Herdr's goto panel (`prefix`+`g`) no
longer lists every Claude Code pane as `claude`.
- Rename a tab or a pane yourself and Auto Title stops touching it. Clear the
name to hand it back.
- On Windows, Herdr reports only the shell or an agent running in a pane, so an
editor or an ssh or mosh session does not name its tab.

Warning

In the default mode, the first start renames every pane, including panes you
had already named by hand. A pane you rename after that is left alone.
Session-only mode also protects existing names at startup.

## Configuration

[Permalink: Configuration](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#configuration)

Every setting is optional. Copy [`config.env.example`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/config.env.example) to
`~/.config/herdr-auto-title/config.env` and uncomment what you need. That path
works on every platform: on Windows it is under `%USERPROFILE%\.config`. Then
[restart](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#restarting): the file is read once at startup.

Two other directories are read, and the first that already holds the file
wins: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, when it is set to an absolute path, comes before
`~/.config`, and `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS or `%APPDATA%` on
Windows comes after it. The config directory that `herdr plugin list` prints is
not read.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_DEBUG` | `false` | Log at DEBUG instead of INFO |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_POLL_MS` | `500` | How often the session is read, in milliseconds |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` | `50` | Longest title, in columns |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_BRANCH_MAX` | `12` | Longest branch in a title, in columns; `0` hides branches |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_DIRECTORY_MAX` | none | Longest directory in a tab title, in columns; `0` hides it where something else names the tab. Pane labels keep theirs |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_POSITION` | `true` | Put the tab's position in front of its title |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MANUAL_FILE` | `manual-names.json`, found the same way | Where names you set by hand are kept; empty keeps them in memory |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_TRANSCRIPT` | `true` | Read an agent's own session files: what it is doing, and where |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_SESSION_ONLY` | `false` | Mirror session names only; keep labels when no usable name is ready |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_NAME` | `false` | Put the agent's name in front of what it is doing |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PANES` | `true` | Name panes as well as tabs |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT` | `false` | Name a tab after its agent pane even while another pane is focused |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PANE_ID` | `false` | Put the pane's Herdr ID in front of its label, as `[w1:p2] api` |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_HANDLE` | `false` | Put the name `herdr agent rename` gave the pane's agent in front of its label, as `driver › api` |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_ICONS` | `false` | Put a Nerd Font 3.0+ icon for what a pane runs in front of labels |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_STATUS` | `false` | Put the tab's agent status in front of its title: `◉` idle, `◐` working, `●` blocked, `✓` done |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_WORKSPACES` | `true` | Report what each workspace's active tab is doing as its `topic` |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_WORKSPACE_MAX_LENGTH` | none: Herdr fits it | Longest topic, in columns |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_CLAUDE_DIRS` | none | Extra Claude config homes to search, `:`-separated |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_HERMES_HOMES` | none | Extra absolute Hermes homes to search, `:`-separated (`;` on Windows), including each home's named profiles |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_FOREIGN_PROCESSES` | none | Programs that own their tab and pane labels, so Auto Title leaves them alone; herdr-mirror's streamer is built in. `:`-separated |

On Windows Herdr reports only the shell or a recognised agent per pane, so this setting and the built-in herdr-mirror check may not detect a label-owning program there.

`HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_TRANSCRIPT=false` also stops Hermes reads and drops the
branch from a tab whose agent works in a git worktree: the transcript is what
names that worktree.

### Session-only mode

[Permalink: Session-only mode](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#session-only-mode)

`HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_SESSION_ONLY=true` names tabs and panes only from the name
their agent session holds: Claude Code's title, Codex's index name, Pi's
session name, Hermes's native title, Antigravity's annotation, Grok Build's
generated title.

- Until a usable name exists, the label stays as it is. No terminal title,
process, directory or opening prompt stands in, even after `/new` or exit.
- Names already set by hand are protected from the first poll. Turning the mode
off keeps them locked; clear a name to hand it back.
- Only Hermes says where its title came from, so another agent's stored name
may still be prompt text.
- Auto Title records the labels it set in `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MANUAL_FILE`, so a
restart does not mistake them for yours. That file therefore holds generated
names too; left empty, nothing survives a restart.

Details are in [title resolution](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/docs/architecture/title-resolution.md#session-only-mode).

### Hermes

[Permalink: Hermes](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#hermes)

Hermes titles are read from `sessions.title` in its `state.db`, read-only: no
chat messages, no LLM call. They need a Herdr integration that reports the
Hermes session ID. Auto Title looks in the foreground process's `HERMES_HOME`
on Linux, then in the plugin's `HERMES_HOME`, `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_HERMES_HOMES`
and `~/.hermes`, each with its `profiles/*`. Paths must be absolute. A session
found in two homes names nothing. Details are in
[Hermes session titles](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/docs/architecture/hermes-session-titles.md).

## Restarting

[Permalink: Restarting](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#restarting)

```
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

This starts a fresh Auto Title in place of the running one, and a notification
says how it went. Run it after an update, after changing the configuration, or
when the plugin has stopped naming tabs.

On Windows the action needs Herdr 0.9.0 or newer. An upgrade from a version
before 0.8.0 needs one `herdr server stop` instead: that instance does not know
to leave.

## About

Automatically name Herdr tabs and panes from your current work: Git branch, running process, and Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, Hermes and Antigravity sessions. No LLM, no external service.

A [Herdr](https://herdr.dev/) plugin that names your tabs and panes from what
they are doing: the Git branch, the running process, or the topic of a Claude
Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, Hermes or Antigravity session. No LLM, no external
service, and a tab you rename yourself stays yours.

## Install

[Permalink: Install](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#install)

You need Herdr 0.8.2+ on macOS, Linux or Windows.

```
herdr plugin install kryptamine/herdr-auto-title --ref stable
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

`stable` is the latest release. On amd64 and arm64 the install downloads its
binary; elsewhere it builds from source with Go 1.24+. On Windows the download
needs Git for Windows' Bash, and Go without it. The second line starts the
plugin now rather than at Herdr's next start.

To update, keeping your configuration:

```
herdr plugin update herdr.auto-title
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

Herdr before 0.9.4 has no `plugin update`; rerun the install lines instead.
An update stays on the ref you installed: a tag never moves, and no `--ref`
follows `main`. To switch, install once with `--ref stable`.

To run the latest commit on `main`, which can be ahead of the latest release,
leave `--ref` out. Herdr then builds from source with Go 1.24+:

```
herdr plugin install kryptamine/herdr-auto-title
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

## Herdr desktop app

[Permalink: Herdr desktop app](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#herdr-desktop-app)

The [desktop app](https://herdr.dev/) has no plugins, so Auto Title runs there
as a service of its own, started at every login on macOS, Linux and Windows.
The mod installs it on all three platforms; Windows needs no Git Bash or Go.

**With the mod:** ask the app's agent to add the mod in this repository's
[`mod/`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/mod) folder, or copy `mod/mods/auto-title` into
`~/.config/herdr-app/mods/` and merge [`mod/keys.json`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/mod/keys.json) into
`~/.config/herdr-app/keys.json` yourself. `cmd-alt-t` opens a popup; press
`Install`. In a tab of its own it downloads the binary of the release the mod
belongs to, checks it against `SHA256SUMS` and has it install itself. The same
popup starts and updates it. Once a day the service asks GitHub whether a
newer release is out, and opens the popup by itself once for each one. To
remove Auto Title, have the service's copy uninstall itself:

```
# macOS
~/Library/Application\ Support/herdr-auto-title/bin/herdr-auto-title desktop uninstall
# Linux
"${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/herdr-auto-title/herdr-auto-title" desktop uninstall
```

**By hand:** with a release binary, or one built with `make build`:

```
./herdr-auto-title desktop install     # start now and at every login
./herdr-auto-title desktop uninstall   # stop it and remove it
```

On Windows the popup prefers Git Bash and uses Windows PowerShell 5.1 when
Git Bash is unavailable. If policy blocks PowerShell scripts, install Git for
Windows or use a release binary directly. No Go installation is needed.

On Windows the binary is `herdr-auto-title.exe`, and the service is a Task
Scheduler task; its copy is
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\herdr-auto-title\bin\herdr-auto-title.exe`, which
`desktop uninstall` removes too.

Installing again is the update. The service runs its own copy of the binary, so
the one you ran can be deleted. Its log is `~/Library/Logs/herdr-auto-title.log`
on macOS and `journalctl --user -u herdr-auto-title` on Linux. On Windows it
keeps no log; run `herdr-auto-title.exe desktop` in a terminal to see one.

What differs from Herdr TUI:

- Only tabs are named: the desktop app has no pane labels or workspace topics.
- The service does not see your shell's environment, so settings go in
[`config.env`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#configuration), never in a shell profile.
- `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_ICONS` needs a Nerd Font as the app's `ui_font` in its
`settings.json`, since the tab bar is drawn in that font.

## Recommended setup

[Permalink: Recommended setup](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#recommended-setup)

Three settings make Auto Title work as intended. Each is optional.

**Create tabs without a name prompt.** Herdr asks for a name before it creates
a tab, and a name typed there counts as your own, so Auto Title never names
that tab. In Herdr's `config.toml`:

```
[ui]
prompt_new_tab_name = false
```

**Install Herdr's integration for each agent you use.** It tells Auto Title
which session a pane holds, so the tab is named after that session. Without it,
a tab says only what the agent puts in its terminal title, and for Antigravity
CLI that is nothing but `agy`.

```
herdr integration install claude           # Claude Code
herdr integration install codex            # Codex
herdr integration install antigravity-cli  # Antigravity CLI
herdr integration install grok             # Grok Build
herdr integration install hermes           # Hermes Agent
herdr integration install pi               # Pi
```

**Show the topic in the sidebar.** Auto Title reports what each workspace's
active tab is doing as `$topic`, and Herdr draws it only where a sidebar row
asks for it. This keeps the name and branch on top, with the topic in bold
under them:

```
[ui.sidebar.spaces]
rows = [\
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "branch", "git_status"],\
  [{ token = "$topic", bold = true, dim = false }],\
]
```

Each client reads its own `config.toml`, so set the rows on every machine you
attach from.

## What you get

[Permalink: What you get](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#what-you-get)

```
~/work/dashboard                       →  1 · dashboard
~/work/dashboard on feature/MC-13200   →  2 · dashboard › MC-13200
nvim editing auth.provider.ts          →  3 · nvim › auth.provider.ts
an agent working on OAuth scopes       →  4 · dashboard › Implement OAuth scopes
ssh into prod-01                       →  5 · ssh › prod-01
mosh into devbox                       →  6 · mosh › devbox
$HOME                                  →  7 · Shell
```

- The number in front is the tab's position, which is also the key that
switches to it.
- The default branch is left out. Other branches are cut down to what
identifies them: `bugfix-asa-cpanel-uapi-mc-13675` becomes `MC-13675`.
- A tab with several panes is named after the pane focused in it, whether the
tab is shown or not. `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT=true` names it after its
agent pane instead.
- Each pane gets a name of its own, so Herdr's goto panel (`prefix`+`g`) no
longer lists every Claude Code pane as `claude`.
- Rename a tab or a pane yourself and Auto Title stops touching it. Clear the
name to hand it back.
- On Windows, Herdr reports only the shell or an agent running in a pane, so an
editor or an ssh or mosh session does not name its tab.

Warning

In the default mode, the first start renames every pane, including panes you
had already named by hand. A pane you rename after that is left alone.
Session-only mode also protects existing names at startup.

## Configuration

[Permalink: Configuration](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#configuration)

Every setting is optional. Copy [`config.env.example`](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/config.env.example) to
`~/.config/herdr-auto-title/config.env` and uncomment what you need. That path
works on every platform: on Windows it is under `%USERPROFILE%\.config`. Then
[restart](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#restarting): the file is read once at startup.

Two other directories are read, and the first that already holds the file
wins: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, when it is set to an absolute path, comes before
`~/.config`, and `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS or `%APPDATA%` on
Windows comes after it. The config directory that `herdr plugin list` prints is
not read.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_DEBUG` | `false` | Log at DEBUG instead of INFO |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_POLL_MS` | `500` | How often the session is read, in milliseconds |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` | `50` | Longest title, in columns |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_BRANCH_MAX` | `12` | Longest branch in a title, in columns; `0` hides branches |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_DIRECTORY_MAX` | none | Longest directory in a tab title, in columns; `0` hides it where something else names the tab. Pane labels keep theirs |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_POSITION` | `true` | Put the tab's position in front of its title |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MANUAL_FILE` | `manual-names.json`, found the same way | Where names you set by hand are kept; empty keeps them in memory |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_TRANSCRIPT` | `true` | Read an agent's own session files: what it is doing, and where |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_SESSION_ONLY` | `false` | Mirror session names only; keep labels when no usable name is ready |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_NAME` | `false` | Put the agent's name in front of what it is doing |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PANES` | `true` | Name panes as well as tabs |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT` | `false` | Name a tab after its agent pane even while another pane is focused |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PANE_ID` | `false` | Put the pane's Herdr ID in front of its label, as `[w1:p2] api` |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_HANDLE` | `false` | Put the name `herdr agent rename` gave the pane's agent in front of its label, as `driver › api` |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_ICONS` | `false` | Put a Nerd Font 3.0+ icon for what a pane runs in front of labels |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_STATUS` | `false` | Put the tab's agent status in front of its title: `◉` idle, `◐` working, `●` blocked, `✓` done |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_WORKSPACES` | `true` | Report what each workspace's active tab is doing as its `topic` |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_WORKSPACE_MAX_LENGTH` | none: Herdr fits it | Longest topic, in columns |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_CLAUDE_DIRS` | none | Extra Claude config homes to search, `:`-separated |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_HERMES_HOMES` | none | Extra absolute Hermes homes to search, `:`-separated (`;` on Windows), including each home's named profiles |
| `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_FOREIGN_PROCESSES` | none | Programs that own their tab and pane labels, so Auto Title leaves them alone; herdr-mirror's streamer is built in. `:`-separated |

On Windows Herdr reports only the shell or a recognised agent per pane, so this setting and the built-in herdr-mirror check may not detect a label-owning program there.

`HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_TRANSCRIPT=false` also stops Hermes reads and drops the
branch from a tab whose agent works in a git worktree: the transcript is what
names that worktree.

### Session-only mode

[Permalink: Session-only mode](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#session-only-mode)

`HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_SESSION_ONLY=true` names tabs and panes only from the name
their agent session holds: Claude Code's title, Codex's index name, Pi's
session name, Hermes's native title, Antigravity's annotation, Grok Build's
generated title.

- Until a usable name exists, the label stays as it is. No terminal title,
process, directory or opening prompt stands in, even after `/new` or exit.
- Names already set by hand are protected from the first poll. Turning the mode
off keeps them locked; clear a name to hand it back.
- Only Hermes says where its title came from, so another agent's stored name
may still be prompt text.
- Auto Title records the labels it set in `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MANUAL_FILE`, so a
restart does not mistake them for yours. That file therefore holds generated
names too; left empty, nothing survives a restart.

Details are in [title resolution](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/docs/architecture/title-resolution.md#session-only-mode).

### Hermes

[Permalink: Hermes](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#hermes)

Hermes titles are read from `sessions.title` in its `state.db`, read-only: no
chat messages, no LLM call. They need a Herdr integration that reports the
Hermes session ID. Auto Title looks in the foreground process's `HERMES_HOME`
on Linux, then in the plugin's `HERMES_HOME`, `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_HERMES_HOMES`
and `~/.hermes`, each with its `profiles/*`. Paths must be absolute. A session
found in two homes names nothing. Details are in
[Hermes session titles](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/blob/main/docs/architecture/hermes-session-titles.md).

## Restarting

[Permalink: Restarting](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title#restarting)

```
herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart
```

This starts a fresh Auto Title in place of the running one, and a notification
says how it went. Run it after an update, after changing the configuration, or
when the plugin has stopped naming tabs.

On Windows the action needs Herdr 0.9.0 or newer. An upgrade from a version
before 0.8.0 needs one `herdr server stop` instead: that instance does not know
to leave.

{"markdown":"# gitview

Review what your agents changed, stage it and commit it, without leaving
Herdr. gitview takes over the Changes panel: it lists the repo's changed
files (staged, unstaged, conflicts; flat or as a tree), and a click opens
the file's diff in a full-height pane beside it. Stage, unstage and discard
with a key or a button, commit from the panel, write review notes on lines
and send them to an agent, and press Enter to edit the file in nvim.

![gitview](preview.png)

## Adding it (for the app's agent)

Don't copy the folders: gitview needs its binary, and it edits the person's
layout (the Changes panel), which copying doesn't do. With the app open,
run its installer:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
```

Tell the person first what it does:

- downloads the prebuilt `herdr-gitview` for this machine from the GitHub
  release, checked against its SHA-256 (macOS and Linux);
- runs programs (`git`, `hc`, `herdr-app`, an editor) and writes to the repo
  only when they stage, discard or commit; no network of its own (a space on
  another machine is reached through herdr-core);
- adds the gitview mods, adds `cmd-shift-g` and `cmd-g` where they are free,
  and points the layout's Changes panel at gitview (on one of Herdr's own
  layouts, a copy of it, which it switches to).

It needs git. Running the installer again upgrades; `--uninstall` takes all
of it out and brings back the stock Changes panel.

structuredContent.markdown:
# gitview

Review what your agents changed, stage it and commit it, without leaving
Herdr. gitview takes over the Changes panel: it lists the repo's changed
files (staged, unstaged, conflicts; flat or as a tree), and a click opens
the file's diff in a full-height pane beside it. Stage, unstage and discard
with a key or a button, commit from the panel, write review notes on lines
and send them to an agent, and press Enter to edit the file in nvim.

![gitview](preview.png)

## Adding it (for the app's agent)

Don't copy the folders: gitview needs its binary, and it edits the person's
layout (the Changes panel), which copying doesn't do. With the app open,
run its installer:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
```

Tell the person first what it does:

- downloads the prebuilt `herdr-gitview` for this machine from the GitHub
  release, checked against its SHA-256 (macOS and Linux);
- runs programs (`git`, `hc`, `herdr-app`, an editor) and writes to the repo
  only when they stage, discard or commit; no network of its own (a space on
  another machine is reached through herdr-core);
- adds the gitview mods, adds `cmd-shift-g` and `cmd-g` where they are free,
  and points the layout's Changes panel at gitview (on one of Herdr's own
  layouts, a copy of it, which it switches to).

It needs git. Running the installer again upgrades; `--uninstall` takes all
of it out and brings back the stock Changes panel.

## What you see

- **The panel** (the layout's `changes` block), drawn like the stock one: a
  42px header with `uncommitted` (or `vs <base>`), the branch in `muted`, an
  `N notes` pill, a bordered `N files` pill with the `+A −D` totals, a
  spinner place that never moves anything, and from 340px wide tree/flat
  and history buttons.
- **The list**: section headers (Merge conflicts, Staged, Changes) with a
  count chip; 28px file rows with the status letter (M `blocked`, A/U
  `ansi2`, D `ansi1`, R `ansi4`), the folder in `dim`, the name, `+adds`
  `ansi2` and `−dels` `ansi1`. Hover `hover`, selected `selected`. On the
  hovered or selected row the counts give way to `+`, `−` and `↺` buttons; a
  hovered section header shows them for all its files. Tree mode adds folder
  rows (chevron, folder icon, file count), a folder holding one folder folded
  into it.
- **The commit row** (uncommitted view): a message box that grows to 8 lines
  and a button: "Commit staged", or "Commit all" with nothing staged.
- **The footer**: the view's most useful keys as keycaps (`[s] stage [u]
  unstage [⏎] nvim …`) and a `?` keycap for the keys card; a message replaces
  them for 5s. The commit row and the footer stay at the panel's bottom,
  also when the list is empty or loading.
- **History** (`l`): commits with subject, refs, short sha, age and author;
  a commit opens its files. **Notes** (`n`): each note's `file:lines` and
  first line.
- **The diff pane**, full height at the tab's right edge, just left of the
  panel: a header (status, path, `+a −d`, a scope tag: `staged`,
  `uncommitted`, `vs <base>` or `commit <sha>`, ×) and the diff in the
  terminal font: line numbers, syntax colors, inserts and deletes tinted
  `ansi2`/`ansi1` at 15% with changed words at 36%, unchanged runs folded
  (`▸ ⋯ N unchanged lines`). The cursor line is a faint full-width band
  with a 2px bar; colors too dim on a tint are lifted to 3.5 contrast.
  Notes show as cards under their lines. A diff longer than 5,000 lines
  ends with "diff cut at 5,000 lines".
- **Preview**, for markdown, images, SVG and HTML: a `Diff | Preview`
  toggle in the header; markdown rendered, an image fitted, a changed image
  before | after side by side.
- **cmd-g's tab** "gitview": the diff on the left, the list on the right.
- **Dialogs**: "Discard changes?" (the app's confirm), "Send N notes to…"
  (the agents, this space's first), the keys card (`?`), and "Save them?"
  when an editor gitview started has unsaved changes.

## How it behaves

- **The panel follows the shown space**: the repo of the focused terminal's
  folder, else the space's. Focusing gitview's diff pane or herdr-nvim's
  nvim keeps the repo. It refreshes on a folder watch; a space on another
  machine is polled every 4s while gitview has the keys, else every 10s.
- **Browsing**: a click, `j`/`k` or the arrows select a file and its diff
  shows at once; the pane opens on the first file clicked and is reused.
  Between files the old diff stays (dimmed after 150ms) until the new one is
  there: the pane never blanks.
- **List keys**: `s` stage, `u` unstage, `x` discard (asks first) the row,
  folder or section; `enter` opens the file in the editor (on a folder:
  folds it); `h`/`←` and `→` fold and unfold; `t` flat or tree; `w`
  uncommitted or vs base; `l` history; `n` notes; `p` send notes; `c` the
  commit message (enter commits, shift-enter a new line, esc leaves it);
  `g`/`G` first and last; `r` refresh; `?` all keys. Chords with cmd, ctrl
  or alt are left to the app.
- **Diff pane keys**: `j`/`k`, page keys, `g`/`G`, the wheel and clicks move
  the cursor; `v` or a drag selects; `a` writes a note on the selection
  (staged or unstaged diffs only); `s`/`u`/`x` act on the shown file; `J`/`K`
  the next or previous file (the list follows); `m` Diff or Preview; `enter`
  the editor at the cursor's line; `esc` clears the selection.
- **Enter → the editor**, which takes the diff pane's place (as v1's diff
  pane became nvim):
  - the editor: herdr-nvim's nvim when it's installed; else an nvim already
    in the tab; else the one configured (`editor` in config.toml, `$VISUAL`,
    `$EDITOR`, nvim, vim, vi), started in a terminal in the diff's place;
    else the system's opener, in its own window; with no editor, a toast
    says what to install;
  - `:q` brings the diff back on that file with the keys on the list; the
    file's row shows `in nvim`, and a click on it brings the diff back too
    (herdr-nvim keeps the buffer; an nvim gitview started quits when clean);
  - moving to another file: herdr-nvim's pane makes way for the new diff
    (the daemon keeps unsaved edits); an nvim gitview started quits when
    clean and its place goes to the new diff, and stays with "editor has
    unsaved changes — stays open" when not; an editor gitview can't ask
    (vim) stays, and its diff comes when it quits;
  - in cmd-g's tab the diff stays, and the editor opens beside it.
- **Discard** asks first. From Changes it keeps a partly staged file's staged
  part.
- **Commit** commits what's staged, else everything (`git add -A`); with
  conflicts it refuses and changes nothing. A slow hook past 30s says "still
  running or timed out: check git log" and keeps the message.
- **Notes** are kept per repo until sent or deleted. Send places them in the
  agent's input as a bracketed paste (no clipboard), or submits them with
  shift-enter; a program without bracketed paste gets nothing and the dialog
  says why.
- **cmd-shift-g** shows the panel with the keys on the list, or hides it.
  Hiding it (also by the Changes or Files button) closes gitview's unit in
  the space: the diff panes, the herdr-nvim pane gitview handed a file to,
  and an editor gitview started (a clean one quits; unsaved changes ask Save,
  Discard or Cancel). Showing it again opens the selected file. **cmd-g**
  opens the gitview tab for the repo, jumps to it, and from inside closes it.
- **One focus**: the list takes the keyboard through `pane.go right`, so
  only one thing looks focused.
- **Tracing**: gitview keeps a trace of what it did for bug reports (no file
  contents, messages, notes or diff text). The palette has "gitview: mark
  (something's wrong)" and "gitview: tracing on/off".

## Built from

- **Layout**: only the `changes` block of the person's personal layout
  changes, to `{mod: "gitview", props: {replaces: <old content>}}`; the tab
  bar's Changes button then shows gitview. On one of Herdr's own layouts the
  installer clones it once (`<name>-copy`) and switches to the copy. Keys go
  in only where free. Uninstall puts `replaces` back and removes only its
  keys; it never deletes or switches a layout. herdr-nvim edits `files` the
  same way, in either order.
- **Mods**:
  - `gitview`: the list, in the panel and in cmd-g's tab (`placement.js`
    decides which from the props);
  - `gitview-diff`: the diff pane (`props: {tab}`), its Preview, and an image
    cache in `mods/gitview-diff/.cache` (hidden, the newest 50 files);
  - `gitview-sidebar` (cmd-shift-g) and `gitview-tab` (cmd-g): one-shot
    launchers;
  - `gitview-agents` (the send dialog), `gitview-ask` (Save them?),
    `gitview-keys` (the keys card), `gitview-mark` and `gitview-tracing`
    (the palette commands).

  Files the mods share are symlinks in the repo; the installer copies them.
- **The list is the only writer of what the pane shows**: shared
  `gitview.views[<tab>]` (the file, section, scope, base or commit, its
  `rev`, a `seq` per write and a `showing` per new file). The pane asks the
  list for s/u/x and J/K (`gitview.ask` / `gitview.answer`) and publishes its
  cursor (`gitview.cursor`). Other shared keys: `gitview.notes`,
  `gitview.handoff` (the file handed to herdr-nvim), `gitview.editors` (the
  editors gitview started), `gitview.discards` (pending discards by token),
  `gitview.changed` (a repo changed). Per-tab keys drop tabs that are gone.
- **The binary** `mods/gitview/bin/herdr-gitview`, paths in
  `mods/gitview/config.json`:
  `json status|diff|file|stage|unstage|discard|commit|log|commit-files|notes|nvim|editor|send|sidebar`
  and `app-setup install|uninstall`. Every repo op takes `--on <machine>`
  (git runs there through `hc exec --on`) and `--root`. The contract is the
  module doc of `src/appjson.rs`.
- **Keys** (`keys.json`): `cmd-shift-g` gitview-sidebar, `cmd-g`
  gitview-tab; on Linux (`keys.linux.json`) `ctrl-alt-shift-g`,
  `ctrl-alt-g`.
- **Install**: `install.sh` at the repo root (release bundle), or
  `herdr-app/install.sh` in a clone (builds from source).

## Watch out

- Read `props()` only in `init` and keep it: in a task resumed by a promise,
  `props()` can belong to another copy (null 3–12% of the time), and the
  pane skipped files.
- Never start work from `render()`: render notices a change and wakes a task
  made in `init`.
- Rows in the app's virtual lists can't have their own handlers, so the list
  is the mod's own scroller (`scroller.js`).
- A hidden copy (the panel's list while the panel is hidden, or any copy in
  a covered window) isn't drawn: the list also looks every 300ms.
- herdr-app 0.1.12–0.1.13 issues with workarounds in the mods:
  - an exec in flight can be dropped when a mod pane or dialog closes; the
    loads treat it as lost and run again (`Loads.revive`), and a confirmed
    discard still running after 1.5s counts as lost;
  - with two copies waiting on `watchFolder` for one folder, only the newest
    wakes; the waking list stamps `gitview.changed` and every list follows
    it;
  - a copy not waiting on `nextCommand()` when a command comes never gets
    it; one task only queues commands;
  - every hot reload keeps the old code for the app's life: the installer
    swaps each changed mod in with one rename and leaves unchanged ones
    alone;
  - `pane.go` does nothing in a window that never drew.
- `terminal.show` can't put a terminal in a mod pane, so the editor's
  terminal opens right of the diff pane and the diff pane closes, in one
  turn; the copy that ran Enter may be the closing diff pane, so the
  editor's record is written first and any copy finds its terminal.
- Swap panes in one turn (open or split the new one off the old one, then
  close the old), or the terminals widen and narrow again.
- herdr-nvim runs in its daemon's folder: don't take its pane's folder as the
  repo.
- `exec` has a 30s limit and no stdin; every call the engine makes to
  herdr-core, herdr-app or nvim has its own deadline.
- macOS is tested end to end; the app version is untested on Linux (the
  release ships a Linux bundle, and CI tests the engine there); Windows
  isn't supported.

## Done when

- `herdr-app check` passes for every gitview mod and `herdr-app status`
  shows no errors.
- The Changes button shows the shown space's changes; a click opens one diff
  pane beside the panel, and j/k, clicks and J/K reuse it, each move showing
  its diff.
- `s`/`u`/`x` and the buttons change exactly what git says; discard asks
  first; the commit row commits the staged files, or everything with none
  staged, and refuses with conflicts.
- History lists commits and a commit's files; notes show as cards and reach
  an agent's input without the clipboard.
- Enter opens the editor at the line; with herdr-nvim, `:q` brings the diff
  back and moving to another file swaps nvim for its diff.
- cmd-shift-g hides the panel with its unit and shows it with the selected
  file; cmd-g opens, jumps to and closes the gitview tab.
- A markdown file opens in Preview; a changed image shows before and after.
- A space on another machine lists, diffs, stages and edits there.
- An agent's write shows in the list within 2s.
- Uninstall brings back the stock Changes panel and leaves keys.json as it
  was.
- `node --test herdr-app/test/*.test.mjs` and the e2e suites
  (`herdr-app/e2e/run.sh`, `coexist.sh`, `follow.sh`, `jank.sh`,
  `reload.sh`, `package.sh`) pass.

{"markdown":"#!/bin/sh
# gitview's installer, for the Herdr desktop app, the herdr TUI, or both:
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
#
#   install.sh [--app] [--tui] [--uninstall] [--version vX.Y.Z] [--bundle FILE]
#
# With neither --app nor --tui: whichever Herdr is installed (both if both).
# Run it again to upgrade.
#
# App: downloads the release's app bundle for this machine (the
# herdr-gitview binary and the mods; no clone, no Rust toolchain), checks it
# against its SHA-256, and runs the bundle's herdr-app/install.sh with the
# app open. --version picks a release (default: the latest), --bundle a
# bundle file instead of a download (its .sha256 beside it is checked).
#
# TUI: `herdr plugin install ChmaraX/herdr-gitview` (or `herdr plugin
# update`); its keys are bound by hand, as TUI.md says.
set -eu

repo=ChmaraX/herdr-gitview
plugin=chmarax.gitview
app= tui= uninstall= version= bundle=
die() { echo "gitview: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "gitview: $*"; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case $1 in
    --app) app=1 ;;
    --tui) tui=1 ;;
    --uninstall) uninstall=1 ;;
    --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--version needs a tag"; version=$2; shift ;;
    --bundle) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--bundle needs a file"; bundle=$2; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,19p' "$0" 2>/dev/null || echo "see https://github.com/$repo#install"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "unknown argument $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done

# The Herdr app: herdr-app on PATH, a Herdr bundle (macOS, by its bundle id),
# or an app home (Linux, or a launch that never put it on PATH).
have_app() {
  command -v herdr-app >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  for b in /Applications/*.app "$HOME"/Applications/*.app; do
    [ -f "$b/Contents/Info.plist" ] || continue
    [ "$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw "$b/Contents/Info.plist" 2>/dev/null)" = dev.herdr.app ] && return 0
  done
  [ -d "${HERDR_APP_HOME:-$HOME/.config/herdr-app}" ]
}
have_tui() { command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1; }

if [ -z "$app$tui" ]; then
  have_app && app=1
  have_tui && tui=1
  [ -n "$app$tui" ] || die "found neither the Herdr app nor the herdr TUI; install one first (https://herdr.dev)"
fi

target() {
  case "$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" in
    Darwin-arm64) echo aarch64-apple-darwin ;;
    Darwin-x86_64) echo x86_64-apple-darwin ;;
    Linux-x86_64) echo x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
    Linux-aarch64|Linux-arm64) echo aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
    *) die "no prebuilt gitview for $(uname -s) $(uname -m); build from source (README: Development)" ;;
  esac
}

sha256() {
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$1"; else sha256sum "$1"; fi | cut -d' ' -f1
}

install_app() {
  work=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
  if [ -n "$bundle" ]; then
    [ -f "$bundle" ] || die "no bundle at $bundle"
    cp "$bundle" "$work/app.tar.gz"
    [ ! -f "$bundle.sha256" ] || cp "$bundle.sha256" "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256"
  else
    name=herdr-gitview-app-$(target).tar.gz
    if [ -n "$version" ]; then base=https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$version
    else base=https://github.com/$repo/releases/latest/download; fi
    say "downloading $name (${version:-latest})"
    curl -fsSL "$base/$name" -o "$work/app.tar.gz" ||
      die "could not download $base/$name (releases before the app bundle have none; build from source: README)"
    curl -fsSL "$base/$name.sha256" -o "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256" || die "could not download $name.sha256"
  fi
  if [ -f "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256" ]; then
    want=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256")
    [ "$(sha256 "$work/app.tar.gz")" = "$want" ] || die "the bundle does not match its SHA-256; nothing installed"
  fi
  tar -xzf "$work/app.tar.gz" -C "$work"
  dir=$(find "$work" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'herdr-gitview-app-*' | head -1)
  [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -x "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" ] || die "the bundle has no bin/herdr-gitview"
  # The binary runs here (`json` with no op answers in JSON); no answer (an
  # older glibc, another architecture) means it can't.
  "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" json 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"error"' ||
    die "the prebuilt herdr-gitview does not run on this machine; build from source (README: Development)"
  bash "$dir/herdr-app/install.sh" --binary "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" ${uninstall:+--uninstall}
}

install_tui() {
  command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "the herdr TUI is not installed (https://herdr.dev)"
  listed=$(herdr plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -F -- "- $plugin " || true)
  if [ -n "$uninstall" ]; then
    [ -n "$listed" ] || { say "the TUI plugin is not installed"; return; }
    herdr plugin uninstall "$plugin"
    say "removed the TUI plugin"
  elif echo "$listed" | grep -q '\[local:'; then
    say "the TUI plugin is linked from a checkout ($listed); left as it is"
  elif [ -n "$listed" ]; then
    herdr plugin update --yes "$plugin"
    say "updated the TUI plugin"
  else
    herdr plugin install --yes "$repo"
    say "installed the TUI plugin; bind its keys in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml (https://github.com/$repo/blob/main/TUI.md#install)"
  fi
}

[ -z "$app" ] || install_app
[ -z "$tui" ] || install_tui

#!/bin/sh
# gitview's installer, for the Herdr desktop app, the herdr TUI, or both:
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --app
#
#   install.sh [--app] [--tui] [--uninstall] [--version vX.Y.Z] [--bundle FILE]
#
# With neither --app nor --tui: whichever Herdr is installed (both if both).
# Run it again to upgrade.
#
# App: downloads the release's app bundle for this machine (the
# herdr-gitview binary and the mods; no clone, no Rust toolchain), checks it
# against its SHA-256, and runs the bundle's herdr-app/install.sh with the
# app open. --version picks a release (default: the latest), --bundle a
# bundle file instead of a download (its .sha256 beside it is checked).
#
# TUI: `herdr plugin install ChmaraX/herdr-gitview` (or `herdr plugin
# update`); its keys are bound by hand, as TUI.md says.
set -eu

repo=ChmaraX/herdr-gitview
plugin=chmarax.gitview
app= tui= uninstall= version= bundle=
die() { echo "gitview: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "gitview: $*"; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case $1 in
    --app) app=1 ;;
    --tui) tui=1 ;;
    --uninstall) uninstall=1 ;;
    --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--version needs a tag"; version=$2; shift ;;
    --bundle) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--bundle needs a file"; bundle=$2; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,19p' "$0" 2>/dev/null || echo "see https://github.com/$repo#install"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "unknown argument $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done

# The Herdr app: herdr-app on PATH, a Herdr bundle (macOS, by its bundle id),
# or an app home (Linux, or a launch that never put it on PATH).
have_app() {
  command -v herdr-app >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  for b in /Applications/*.app "$HOME"/Applications/*.app; do
    [ -f "$b/Contents/Info.plist" ] || continue
    [ "$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw "$b/Contents/Info.plist" 2>/dev/null)" = dev.herdr.app ] && return 0
  done
  [ -d "${HERDR_APP_HOME:-$HOME/.config/herdr-app}" ]
}
have_tui() { command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1; }

if [ -z "$app$tui" ]; then
  have_app && app=1
  have_tui && tui=1
  [ -n "$app$tui" ] || die "found neither the Herdr app nor the herdr TUI; install one first (https://herdr.dev)"
fi

target() {
  case "$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" in
    Darwin-arm64) echo aarch64-apple-darwin ;;
    Darwin-x86_64) echo x86_64-apple-darwin ;;
    Linux-x86_64) echo x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
    Linux-aarch64|Linux-arm64) echo aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
    *) die "no prebuilt gitview for $(uname -s) $(uname -m); build from source (README: Development)" ;;
  esac
}

sha256() {
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$1"; else sha256sum "$1"; fi | cut -d' ' -f1
}

install_app() {
  work=$(mktemp -d)
  trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
  if [ -n "$bundle" ]; then
    [ -f "$bundle" ] || die "no bundle at $bundle"
    cp "$bundle" "$work/app.tar.gz"
    [ ! -f "$bundle.sha256" ] || cp "$bundle.sha256" "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256"
  else
    name=herdr-gitview-app-$(target).tar.gz
    if [ -n "$version" ]; then base=https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$version
    else base=https://github.com/$repo/releases/latest/download; fi
    say "downloading $name (${version:-latest})"
    curl -fsSL "$base/$name" -o "$work/app.tar.gz" ||
      die "could not download $base/$name (releases before the app bundle have none; build from source: README)"
    curl -fsSL "$base/$name.sha256" -o "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256" || die "could not download $name.sha256"
  fi
  if [ -f "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256" ]; then
    want=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$work/app.tar.gz.sha256")
    [ "$(sha256 "$work/app.tar.gz")" = "$want" ] || die "the bundle does not match its SHA-256; nothing installed"
  fi
  tar -xzf "$work/app.tar.gz" -C "$work"
  dir=$(find "$work" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'herdr-gitview-app-*' | head -1)
  [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -x "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" ] || die "the bundle has no bin/herdr-gitview"
  # The binary runs here (`json` with no op answers in JSON); no answer (an
  # older glibc, another architecture) means it can't.
  "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" json 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"error"' ||
    die "the prebuilt herdr-gitview does not run on this machine; build from source (README: Development)"
  bash "$dir/herdr-app/install.sh" --binary "$dir/bin/herdr-gitview" ${uninstall:+--uninstall}
}

install_tui() {
  command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "the herdr TUI is not installed (https://herdr.dev)"
  listed=$(herdr plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -F -- "- $plugin " || true)
  if [ -n "$uninstall" ]; then
    [ -n "$listed" ] || { say "the TUI plugin is not installed"; return; }
    herdr plugin uninstall "$plugin"
    say "removed the TUI plugin"
  elif echo "$listed" | grep -q '\[local:'; then
    say "the TUI plugin is linked from a checkout ($listed); left as it is"
  elif [ -n "$listed" ]; then
    herdr plugin update --yes "$plugin"
    say "updated the TUI plugin"
  else
    herdr plugin install --yes "$repo"
    say "installed the TUI plugin; bind its keys in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml (https://github.com/$repo/blob/main/TUI.md#install)"
  fi
}

[ -z "$app" ] || install_app
[ -z "$tui" ] || install_tui

== build.mjs
// Builds the mod folder dist/gitdeck/: one bundled main.js plus mod.json and assets.
// One file means one reload when installed (each reload keeps old code alive in herdr-app 0.1.x).
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { cp, mkdir, readFile, rm } from "node:fs/promises";

const out = "dist/gitdeck";
const { version } = JSON.parse(await readFile("package.json", "utf8"));

await rm(out, { recursive: true, force: true });
await mkdir(out, { recursive: true });

await build({
  entryPoints: ["src/main.ts"],
  outfile: `${out}/main.js`,
  bundle: true,
  format: "esm",
  target: "es2022",
  platform: "neutral",
  // Provided by the Herdr runtime.
  external: ["herdr", "gpui-kit", "gpui-base", "gpui", "gpui-shell", "fs/promises"],
  // The installed version, for the update check (src/updater.ts).
  define: { __GITDECK_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(version) },
  legalComments: "none",
  logLevel: "warning",
});

await cp("mod/mod.json", `${out}/mod.json`);
await cp("mod/icons", `${out}/icons`, { recursive: true });
process.stdout.write(`build: ${out}\n`);

import { build } from "esbuild";
import { cp, mkdir, readFile, rm } from "node:fs/promises";

const out = "dist/gitdeck";
const { version } = JSON.parse(await readFile("package.json", "utf8"));

await rm(out, { recursive: true, force: true });
await mkdir(out, { recursive: true });

await build({
  entryPoints: ["src/main.ts"],
  outfile: `${out}/main.js`,
  bundle: true,
  format: "esm",
  target: "es2022",
  platform: "neutral",
  // Provided by the Herdr runtime.
  external: ["herdr", "gpui-kit", "gpui-base", "gpui", "gpui-shell", "fs/promises"],
  // The installed version, for the update check (src/updater.ts).
  define: { __GITDECK_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(version) },
  legalComments: "none",
  logLevel: "warning",
});

await cp("mod/mod.json", `${out}/mod.json`);
await cp("mod/icons", `${out}/icons`, { recursive: true });
process.stdout.write(`build: ${out}\n`);

content.text:
✅ MoAI-Easy ★ 다 됐어요 ──────────────────────
🎯 Goal: Herdr mod을 다른 언어로 만들 수 있는지 분석하고, gitdeck에 맞는 선택을 추천하는 보고서
📁 Files: 코드는 하나도 바꾸지 않았습니다. `git status`가 작업 시작 때와 같습니다.
🧪 Proof: 아래 "직접 측정한 것"에 명령과 출력을 적었습니다.
──────────────────────────────────────────────

## 결론

**TypeScript를 그대로 유지하길 권합니다.** Rust나 Go로 mod 전체를 만드는 길은 막혀 있습니다. 대신 JS가 UI를 그리고 Rust·Go 바이너리가 일을 하는 혼합 구조는 가능합니다. 그런데 gitdeck에는 그 이득이 비용보다 작습니다.

## 1. Herdr는 mod를 어떻게 불러오나

**확인한 사실**
- mod는 JavaScript입니다. `main.js`가 `View` 클래스를 export하면, 화면 요소(GPUI element)를 *설명*만 하고 Rust 쪽이 실제로 그립니다 (`~/.config/herdr-app/AGENTS.md` 39~47행).
- 이 저장소의 `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`는 실행 환경을 QuickJS(아주 작은 JS 엔진)로 적고 있습니다. Herdr 자체 문서에는 이 이름이 없고, 이 저장소 문서에만 있는 내용입니다.
- `herdr.d.ts`와 `gpui-kit.d.ts`에서 wasm, native, ffi, dylib를 찾아봤지만 mod 로딩과 관련된 항목이 없었습니다.
- 임시 폴더의 mod를 `herdr-app check`(herdr-app 0.1.15)로 돌려 봤더니 `typeof WebAssembly`가 `undefined`였습니다.
- 외부 프로그램은 `exec(cmd, args, {cwd, on, timeout})`로 실행합니다. 기본 30초, 최대 10분, 출력 8 MiB, stdin 없음입니다. 문서도 "mod는 신뢰된 코드이고 명령·네트워크가 제한 없다"고 명시합니다.

**결론**: Herdr가 직접 불러오는 것은 JS뿐입니다. WASM이나 네이티브 플러그인 로딩 경로는 문서에도 런타임에도 없었습니다. Rust·Go는 `exec`로 부르는 별도 프로그램으로만 쓸 수 있습니다.

## 2. 다른 사람들은 무엇으로 만드나

**확인한 사실** (GitHub 토픽 `herdr-mod`, 2026-11-13 기준 695개 저장소)

| 대표 언어 | 개수 | 비율 |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | 595 | 약 86% |
| Python | 45 | 약 6% |
| **Rust** | **18** | **약 2.6%** |
| **Go** | **15** | **약 2.2%** |
| TypeScript | 14 | 약 2% |

Rust mod가 많다는 인상은 사실과 다릅니다. 압도적으로 JS입니다.

실제로 열어 본 두 사례는 둘 다 "JS 껍데기 + 별도 바이너리" 구조입니다.
- **herdr-gitview** (Rust 68%, JS 20%). gitdeck와 같은 종류의 git 패널입니다. UI는 JS mod 여러 개가 그리고, 일은 `mods/gitview/bin/herdr-gitview` 바이너리가 `status`, `diff`, `stage`, `commit` 같은 하위 명령으로 처리합니다. JS가 `exec`로 호출하는 구조입니다. 설치는 OS·CPU별 바이너리를 내려받아 SHA-256을 확인하는 스크립트이고, macOS(arm64·x64)와 Linux(x64·arm64)만 지원합니다. Windows는 미지원입니다. RECIPE.md에는 "폴더를 복사하지 말고 설치 스크립트를 쓰라"고 적혀 있습니다.
- **herdr-auto-title** (Go). 데스크톱용 JS mod가 릴리스 바이너리를 내려받아 SHA256SUMS를 확인한 뒤 `desktop install`을 실행합니다. `exec`의 30초 제한 때문에 설치를 별도 탭에서 돌린다고 커밋 메시지에 적혀 있습니다.

**한계**: Rust·Go 33개 중 위 둘만 열어 봤습니다. 이 토픽에는 데스크톱 앱 mod 외에 herdr TUI(터미널판) 플러그인과 layout도 섞여 있고, 두 사례는 `herdr-plugin.toml`을 가진 TUI 플러그인도 겸합니다. 나머지 Rust·Go가 어느 쪽인지는 확인하지 못했습니다.

## 3. 비교

| 항목 | TS 유지 | Rust 엔진 + JS UI | Go 엔진 + JS UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| 성능 | 병목은 git 프로세스 기동입니다. 측정은 안 했습니다 | 큰 diff 파싱·그래프 계산에서 이득이 *있을 수 있음* (추측) | Rust와 비슷 (추측) |
| 배포 | `main.js` 하나(202 KB), OS 무관 | OS·CPU별 빌드 4종 이상, 설치 스크립트 필요 | 같음 |
| 자동 업데이트 | 지금 방식 그대로 동작 | JS와 바이너리의 버전을 같이 맞춰야 함 | 같음 |
| 테스트 | 326개 통과, 이미 구축 | 엔진 테스트 재작성, JS UI는 계속 별도 | 같음 |
| 이전 작업량 | 없음 | 엔진 이전 + JSON 계약 + CI + 설치기, 두 언어 유지 | 같음 |
| 보안 | 읽을 수 있는 JS만 설치 | 서명 안 된 바이너리를 내려받아 실행 | 같음 |

**근거**
- **성능**: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`가 git 호출이 대부분임을 보여 줍니다. 언어를 바꿔도 git 자체의 시간은 줄지 않습니다. 이득이 있다면 JS에서 하는 파싱 쪽인데, 실제로 느린지는 재 보지 않았습니다.
- **배포**: `scripts/build.mjs`가 `dist/gitdeck/main.js` 하나를 만듭니다(202 KB 측정). 바이너리가 생기면 gitview처럼 OS별 빌드와 체크섬이 필요합니다. macOS 빌드를 위해 `macos-15`와 `macos-15-intel` 러너를 따로 쓴 사례가 있습니다.
- **업데이트**: `src/updater.ts`는 하루 한 번 GitHub 릴리스를 확인하고, 클릭하면 tar.gz를 받아 `herdr-app check`로 검사한 뒤 한 번의 `mv`로 교체합니다. JS 파일만 바꾸는 구조라서 바이너리가 끼면 다시 설계해야 합니다. 읽은 범위(1~80행)에는 체크섬 검증이 없습니다.
- **테스트**: 아래 측정 참고. 이전하면 `src/core`의 순수 로직은 옮기기 쉬운 구조입니다. 하지만 `ui/`와 `main.ts`는 JS로 남고, 그쪽은 `herdr-app check`와 스크린샷으로만 확인합니다.
- **보안**: AGENTS.md는 외부 mod를 추가할 때 "모든 파일을 읽고, 네트워크·프로그램 실행 여부를 알리라"고 합니다. 바이너리는 이 절차로 읽을 수 없습니다(제 해석입니다). 이 워크로드에서는 JS도 Go도 Rust도 메모리 안전성 차이가 실익이 아닙니다.

**직접 측정한 것**
```
pnpm test      → tests 326 / pass 326 / fail 0 / 3.86초
pnpm coverage  → all files: lines 99.70 / branches 94.98 / funcs 98.25
find src -name '*.ts' | wc → 7,348줄 (tests 3,871줄)
```

## 4. 추천

**TypeScript 유지.** 이유 세 가지입니다.
1. 지금 구조(JS 한 파일, 하루 한 번 점검, 원자적 교체)가 Herdr의 설치·갱신 방식과 정확히 맞습니다. 바이너리를 넣으면 이 장점이 사라집니다.
2. 성능 문제가 실제로 있다는 증거가 아직 없습니다. 같은 종류의 mod 중 git-graph, Better Changes, Redline은 JS입니다(언어 표시만 확인).
3. 이전의 대가는 두 언어 유지, OS별 빌드, 보안 면적 증가입니다.

**다시 검토할 신호**: 거대한 저장소(커밋 수만 개 이상)에서 JS 파싱이 체감될 만큼 느리거나, `exec`의 30초·8 MiB 제한에 실제로 걸릴 때입니다. 그때도 전체를 옮기지 말고 병목 한 곳만 작은 바이너리로 빼는 편이 낫습니다. 굳이 고르면 단일 정적 바이너리라 교차 빌드가 쉬운 Go가 유리해 보이지만, 이건 일반 지식이고 이 조사로 검증한 것은 아닙니다.

## 확인하지 못한 것 (추측으로 남은 부분)
- Rust·Go 엔진이 실제로 몇 배 빠른지: 벤치마크를 하지 않았습니다.
- `exec` 한 번의 기동 비용: 재지 않았습니다.
- 내려받은 바이너리가 macOS Gatekeeper(서명 검사)에서 막히는지: 확인하지 않았습니다.
- QuickJS가 WASM을 지원하는지: Herdr 런타임에서 `WebAssembly`가 없는 것만 확인했습니다.

Sources:
- [GitHub 토픽 herdr-mod](https://github.com/topics/herdr-mod): 언어별 개수 (2026-11-13 조회)
- [herdr.dev/mods](https://herdr.dev/mods): 공개 갤러리 목록
- [ChmaraX/herdr-gitview](https://github.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview): Rust 비율, 설치법, 지원 OS
- [herdr-gitview RECIPE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/herdr-app/RECIPE.md): JS mod가 바이너리를 `exec`로 부르는 구조
- [herdr-gitview install.sh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChmaraX/herdr-gitview/main/install.sh): OS별 바이너리, SHA-256 검증

# Developing gitdeck

## Layout

```
src/
  core/            pure logic, no Herdr imports: tested with Node
    git/runner.ts    the only place git runs (createGit over an injected exec)
    git/status.ts    `git status --porcelain=v2` parser and summary
    repos/discover.ts  find the herd root, list repos below it
    scan.ts          scanHerd / loadStatus (git + find, injected)
    herd.ts          the panel's state: immutable, every change returns a new one
    context.ts       which folder to follow (focus → tab terminal → space)
    paths.ts pool.ts signal.ts   small helpers
  ui/              views: functions from state to gpui-kit elements
  main.ts          the View: wires Herdr's live data, the git task and the views
mod/               mod.json and icons, copied next to the bundle
scripts/           build (esbuild), dev-install (atomic swap), sync-types
tests/             node:test, including real git/find integration tests
```

## Loop

```sh
pnpm test        # node --test (Node runs the .ts directly)
pnpm coverage    # same, failing under 80% lines/branches/functions of src/core
pnpm typecheck   # the mod against the app's types, and the tests
pnpm dev         # build, `herdr-app check` in a hidden folder, swap in
pnpm verify      # typecheck + coverage + build
```

Write the test first. Logic goes in `src/core` behind injected `Git`/`Exec`, so
it can be tested without Herdr; `src/ui` stays thin. After `pnpm dev`, look at
it: `herdr-app shot /tmp/x.png`, and `herdr-app status` must show no errors.
Commands reach a shown copy: `herdr-app do gitdeck.picker`.

## Herdr rules that bite

- Herdr runs **`main.js` only** (QuickJS): TypeScript is bundled by esbuild
  into one file. `herdr`, `gpui-kit`, `gpui-base` are provided at run time
  (externals). No Node APIs, no `setTimeout`, no DOM.
- **Never keep a `cx`.** Every callback and task gets its own.
- **Never start work in `render()`.** It notices a change (`notice()`) and
  fires the `Signal` that the git task started in `init` waits on.
- `.when(cond, …)` needs a real boolean.
- `exec`: an argument array (no shell), 30 s limit, 8 MiB output, **no stdin**.
  Anything that needs input writes a file first (`writeTextFile`, under
  `~/.config/herdr-app`). Long operations (clone, big push) belong in a
  terminal (`hc`), not `exec`.
- Every git call uses `--no-optional-locks`, so gitdeck never blocks an
  agent's git in the same repo.
- Each saved file reloads the mod, and herdr-app 0.1.x keeps old code alive per
  reload: install with `scripts/dev-install.sh` (one rename), never by copying
  files one at a time.
- A command sent while a freshly reloaded copy isn't yet waiting on
  `nextCommand()` is lost; send it again.
- `types/` comes from the installed app (`pnpm types`) and isn't committed:
  it must match the app version you run.

## Release (later)

Semver in `package.json`; tag `vX.Y.Z`; a GitHub release with the built
`dist/gitdeck` folder. For herdr.dev/mods: a public repo with the topic
`herdr-mod`, a `RECIPE.md` and a `preview.png`.

# Skill Routing Protocol

Canonical rule for dynamic skill chaining: how the orchestrator routes domain skills into agent spawns, and how agents load conditional skills on demand.

## 1. Orchestrator Obligation

[ZONE:Evolvable] [HARD] Before spawning an implementation or review `Agent()`, the orchestrator MUST match the mission's domain against the available `moai-ref-*` / `moai-domain-*` skill descriptions and inject an explicit instruction into the spawn prompt for each matched skill (0-3 matches maximum):

```
At start, invoke Skill("<name>") for <reason>.
```

Examples:
- Backend API implementation → `At start, invoke Skill("moai-ref-api-patterns") for REST endpoint and error-handling conventions.`
- Security-sensitive review → `At start, invoke Skill("moai-ref-owasp-checklist") for the OWASP Top 10 review baseline.`
- React/Next.js work → `At start, invoke Skill("moai-ref-react-patterns") for component and state-management patterns.`

When no skill description matches the mission's domain, inject nothing — zero matches is a valid outcome, not a gap.

### §1.1 — Orchestrator-Direct Skill Routing (non-spawn)

[ZONE:Evolvable] [HARD] The §1 obligation binds agent **spawns**. When the orchestrator performs a task **directly** (no `Agent()` spawn) whose output shape matches a `moai-domain-*` skill, the orchestrator MUST load that skill via `Skill()` before producing the artifact. Discovery is mandatory when the task shape matches; the skill body is paid only on invocation (progressive disclosure), so there is no cost to loading it preemptively and failing to match.

| Orchestrator-direct task | Mandatory skill |
|---|---|
| Render a report / markdown → HTML artifact | `moai-domain-html-report` (mode by report type — status/incident/plan/explainer/financial/pr; audience tier from active output style) |
| Humanize / post-edit AI text (de-AI, 윤문) | `moai-domain-humanize` |
| Generate an SVG infographic / architecture diagram | `moai-domain-svg-infographic` |
| Reproduce or capture the look of an existing reference design (screenshot, image set, or URL) — extract it into a Design DNA profile, or generate an artifact from one | `moai-domain-design-dna` |
| Render a data visualization (chart/dashboard) to HTML/SVG | `dataviz` |
| Author a design artifact hosted as a claude.ai web page (visual identity, landing page) | `artifact-design` |

Config coupling (report): the orchestrator reads `report.format` from the settings chain (`.moai/config/sections/report.yaml`, persisted via `internal/settings` — values `html+md` \| `md`) before rendering any report. When the format is `html+md` or `html`, an orchestrator-direct report request MUST route through `moai-domain-html-report`; when `md`, the orchestrator MUST NOT invoke the skill (markdown is the native output, the skill is idle).

[ZONE:Evolvable] [HARD] **Routing is intent-based, not keyword-based**: the orchestrator LLM reads skill descriptions semantically and matches the intent of a request against the described capability, so a single concise English intent statement suffices across all supported conversation languages (CLAUDE.md §2 — intent analysis is language-independent, never gated on English keyword matching). Multi-locale trigger-phrase enumeration in skill descriptions has no basis in this semantic-match mechanism and wastes the 1,536-char listing budget.

[ZONE:Evolvable] [HARD] **Anti-pattern (named)**: reaching for `artifact-design` when the task is a markdown→HTML **report render**. `artifact-design` calibrates visual identity for claude.ai-hosted web pages (landing pages, apps, shareable artifacts); `moai-domain-html-report` owns the report-render surface (six report modes, audience tiers, md-twin asymmetry). A report request that loads `artifact-design` instead of `moai-domain-html-report` is a routing miss. The corrective is intent-based: any request — in any language — whose intent is "produce a report/document as HTML" routes to `moai-domain-html-report`; `artifact-design` routes only "produce a hosted visual-identity page" intents.

## 2. Agent Obligation

Agents whose `tools:` include `Skill` load conditional skills per the "Conditional Skill Loading" section in their own body. The static `skills:` frontmatter preload stays at most 2 entries per agent (token diet — progressive disclosure does the rest). An agent loads a conditional skill when its body's stated trigger situation actually arises, not preemptively.

## 3. Rationale

The two loading mechanisms have different cost profiles:

- `skills:` frontmatter injects each listed skill's FULL body into the agent context at spawn — a fixed cost paid on every invocation, whether or not the skill is used.
- `Skill()` invocation loads on demand: only the ~100-token metadata line is always visible; the ~5K-token body is paid only when the skill is actually invoked.

Keeping the static preload minimal and routing the rest through explicit `Skill()` instructions converts a fixed per-spawn cost into a pay-per-use cost, while the orchestrator-side injection (section 1) preserves discoverability for domain skills the agent would not know to load.

## 4. Cross-references

- `.claude/rules/moai/core/moai-constitution.md` § Agent Core Behaviors — cross-cutting agent obligations
- `.claude/rules/moai/development/agent-authoring.md` — agent frontmatter format (`skills:` YAML array, `tools:` CSV) and the Extension-Mechanism Context-Cost Ladder
- `CLAUDE.md` §4 — the retained agent catalog this protocol applies to
- `.claude/rules/moai/development/skill-authoring.md` § Progressive Disclosure — the 3-level token budget behind the on-demand cost profile

6

8	
9	```
10	At start, invoke Skill("<name>") for <reason>.
11	```
12

14	- Backend API implementation → `At start, invoke Skill("moai-ref-api-patterns") for REST endpoint and error-handling conventions.`
15	- Security-sensitive review → `At start, invoke Skill("moai-ref-owasp-checklist") for the OWASP Top 10 review baseline.`
16	- React/Next.js work → `At start, invoke Skill("moai-ref-react-patterns") for component and state-management patterns.`
17	
18	When no skill description matches the mission's domain, inject nothing — zero matches is a valid outcome, not a gap.
19

21

When the orchestrator performs a task **directly** (no `Agent()` spawn) whose output shape matches a `moai-domain-*` skill, the orchestrator MUST load that skill via `Skill()` before producing the artifact. Discovery is mandatory when the task shape matches; the skill body is paid only on invocation (progressive disclosure), so there is no cost to loading it preemptively and failing to match.
23

25	|---|---|
26	| Render a report / markdown → HTML artifact | `moai-domain-html-report` (mode by report type — status/incident/plan/explainer/financial/pr; audience tier from active output style) |

29	| Reproduce or capture the look of an existing reference design (screenshot, image set, or URL) — extract it into a Design DNA profile, or generate an artifact from one | `moai-domain-design-dna` |
30	| Render a data visualization (chart/dashboard) to HTML/SVG | `dataviz` |
31	| Author a design artifact hosted as a claude.ai web page (visual identity, landing page) | `artifact-design` |

When the format is `html+md` or `html`, an orchestrator-direct report request MUST route through `moai-domain-html-report`; when `md`, the orchestrator MUST NOT invoke the skill (markdown is the native output, the skill is idle).
34

Multi-locale trigger-phrase enumeration in skill descriptions has no basis in this semantic-match mechanism and wastes the 1,536-char listing budget.
36

A report request that loads `artifact-design` instead of `moai-domain-html-report` is a routing miss. The corrective is intent-based: any request — in any language — whose intent is "produce a report/document as HTML" routes to `moai-domain-html-report`; `artifact-design` routes only "produce a hosted visual-identity page" intents.

40

The static `skills:` frontmatter preload stays at most 2 entries per agent (token diet — progressive disclosure does the rest). An agent loads a conditional skill when its body's stated trigger situation actually arises, not preemptively.
42

44	
45	The two loading mechanisms have different cost profiles:
46	
47	- `skills:` frontmatter injects each listed skill's FULL body into the agent context at spawn — a fixed cost paid on every invocation, whether or not the skill is used.
